analysisStatic.supervisionTarget: Identify concrete input-to-bug paths, mitigations, and the exact runtime facts still needed to prove leak and exploitability.
requiredEvidence: binary protections
resolved input entry point and input-to-code path
single strongest input-connected target
specific vulnerable operation or missing bound
candidate leak or no-leak-needed hypothesis
PIE/libc base leak requirement only when addresses from that region are used
heap allocator/libc version constraints when heap primitives are involved
candidate control-flow or direct flag-read route
preferred route order: system('/bin/sh'), one_gadget, then ORW/direct flag read
minimal dynamic proof requirements
analysisStatic.outputContract: Return exactly one raw pwnautomator.analysis.static.v1 JSON object with protections, targets, and exploit_requirements. exploit_requirements must name the leak/base facts only when the exploit uses addresses from that region, explicitly mark PIE/libc as not needed when applicable, include heap allocator/libc version constraints when relevant, and include control-flow/direct-read facts that dynamic analysis must prove. Do not include markdown or code fences.
successCriteria: exploit requirements include leak/control proof requirements
analysisStatic.failurePolicy: When evidence is insufficient, record uncertainty in the target reason; do not invent dynamic facts.
analysisStatic.artifactPolicy: No runtime execution, payload code, or host file writes.

analysisDynamic.supervisionTarget: Prove the selected static target has a usable leak/base route and a control-flow or direct flag-read route before exploit code is written.
requiredEvidence: selected target reference
confirmed leak/base source only when needed or explicit no-leak-needed proof
leak parsing method and offset/base calculation when a leak is needed
confirmed PIE base leak only when PIE addresses are used
confirmed libc base leak only when libc addresses are used
confirmed heap allocator/libc version constraints when heap primitives are used
confirmed control-flow/direct flag-read path
runner-compatible launch assumptions
final route chosen in priority order: system('/bin/sh'), one_gadget, then ORW/direct flag read
only facts needed to write or repair the exploit
explicit blocker only when no route can be proven
analysisDynamic.outputContract: Return exactly one raw pwnautomator.analysis.dynamic.v1 JSON object with runtime_facts. runtime_facts must include observations, primitives, blockers, and exploitability: {status, leak:{status,method,evidence}, control:{status,method,evidence}, exploit_plan:[...]}. Each observation kind must be one of: control, leak, offset, crash, blocker. Use only targeted debugger checks; do not spray breakpoints or use external file-backed GDB command/input workflows. Do not confirm routes that require debugger-only disabled ASLR, fixed PIE bases, custom argv padding, altered environment variables, or launch arguments unavailable to pwn_payload_execute. Do not include exploit code, markdown, or code fences.
successCriteria: every observation is tied to a selected static target
leak is confirmed or proven unnecessary
route is reproducible by pwn_payload_execute runner assumptions
analysisDynamic.failurePolicy: If a candidate cannot be exercised, keep analysis focused on proving an alternative leak/control route. Only report a blocker when no exploit route can be proven from the selected target.
analysisDynamic.artifactPolicy: No exploit payload writes, session commands, or host file writes.

analysisDynamicPoc.supervisionTarget: Confirm, purely through debugger observation, why a provided reference exploit succeeds against this binary -- never by copying or paraphrasing the reference. Used only as a fallback after an unguided exploit/repair attempt window exhausts its turn budget.
requiredEvidence: selected target reference
debugger-confirmed leak/base source or explicit no-leak-needed proof
debugger-confirmed control-flow or direct flag-read path
every fact traced to a live debugger observation, never to the reference exploit's own comments
analysisDynamicPoc.outputContract: Return exactly one raw pwnautomator.analysis.dynamic.v1 JSON object with runtime_facts. Each observation kind must be one of: control, leak, offset, crash, blocker. Every observation must cite a debugger-confirmed fact. Never copy code, offsets, or comments directly from the reference exploit without independently confirming them via the debugger. Do not include exploit code, markdown, or code fences.
successCriteria: every observation is tied to a selected static target
leak is confirmed or proven unnecessary
analysisDynamicPoc.failurePolicy: If the reference route cannot be confirmed via the debugger, report the blocker instead of asserting the reference's claims unverified.
analysisDynamicPoc.artifactPolicy: No exploit payload writes, session commands, or host file writes. Verification only; the reference exploit is never copied into any output.

exploit.supervisionTarget: Use the validated leak/base and control-route proof from static and dynamic artifacts to write the exploit, then iterate until shell or flag access is verified.
requiredEvidence: validated input entry point and vulnerability mechanism
confirmed leak/no-leak-needed proof
confirmed PIE base leak only when PIE addresses are used
confirmed libc base leak only when libc addresses are used
version-compatible heap strategy when heap primitives are used
confirmed control-flow/direct flag-read route
route chosen in priority order: system('/bin/sh'), one_gadget, then ORW/direct flag read
offset/leak/base derivation when needed
payload write and execution evidence
post-exploit command or flag verification
exploit.outputContract: Use concise reasoning and MCP calls. Iterate with focused pwn_payload_write and execution attempts until command or flag verification succeeds, or an external blocker stops the turn.
successCriteria: uid/gid command output or direct flag evidence
exploit.failurePolicy: Do not repeat unchanged payloads. Use each observed failure to make the next focused correction.
exploit.artifactPolicy: Write active challenge hack.py via pwn_payload_write only; dashboard mirrors it to exploit.py.

repair.supervisionTarget: After exploit failure, prove the concrete failure cause with focused output/static/dynamic evidence, then make the smallest payload repair and verify shell or flag access.
requiredEvidence: previous failure
root-cause evidence from execution output, focused static recheck, or focused dynamic debugging
identified failure point: leak parsing, base calculation, offset, alignment, gadget constraint, I/O synchronization, heap state, syscall arguments, or control-flow assumption
changed payload
payload write and execution evidence
post-repair command or flag verification
repair.outputContract: State the current failure hypothesis briefly, then prove or disprove it with the smallest necessary analysis path: execution output, focused Ghidra static recheck, focused debugger attach, or an optional diagnostic payload that prints [MCP][PID] with p.pid and pauses. Do not modify the payload until the failure cause is identified. After root cause proof, make focused pwn_payload_write repairs and verify command or flag success.
successCriteria: uid/gid command output or direct flag evidence
repair.failurePolicy: Do not repeat unchanged payloads. Each further failure must produce a new correction based on fresh evidence.
repair.artifactPolicy: Write active challenge hack.py via pwn_payload_write only; dashboard mirrors it to exploit.py.

promptConstraints: Think, reason, and respond in English only. Do not write Korean or mixed-language explanations.
Use only dashboard-provided MCP tools. Do not use shell commands, local CLI tools, host file writes, external command/input files, or unmanaged process execution.
Do not read /proc/<pid>/maps, /proc/<pid>/mem, or similar procfs process memory paths. Do not use p.libs() or pwntools mapping helpers for base addresses.
Treat each phase contract, tool allowlist, and payload safety rule as mandatory. The dashboard ends a turn that violates them.
Never invent an offset, leak, base, or success result. Report an MCP blocker or an explicit uncertainty instead.

Exploit code must start only after analysis decides the exploit direction: input entry point, vulnerability primitive, leak/no-leak-needed proof, required offsets/bases, and control-flow or direct flag-read route.
Prefer exploit routes in this order when evidence supports them: system('/bin/sh'), one_gadget, then ORW/direct flag read.
Treat ASLR as always enabled. Leak PIE or libc base only when the exploit uses addresses from that region; otherwise explicitly use a no-leak-needed path.
Do not confirm exploit routes that depend on debugger-only disabled ASLR, fixed PIE bases, custom argv padding, altered environment variables, or launch arguments unavailable to pwn_payload_execute.

For heap exploits, choose a strategy compatible with the observed libc/glibc allocator version and hardening, including tcache, safe-linking, hook availability, bin checks, and removed legacy primitives.
Do not declare exploit success from a marker alone. Verify uid/gid command output through pwn_session_send plus pwn_session_poll, or verify direct flag output.
MCP servers are started by the dashboard runtime; do not start or restart them from this task.
compactPromptConstraints: Think, reason, and respond in English only.
Use only the current phase's dashboard MCP tools and respect payload safety rules.
Do not use shell commands, pwncli, /proc/<pid>/maps, /proc/<pid>/mem, p.libs(), external command/input files, GDB file redirection, or unmanaged process wrappers.

ASLR is always on; PIE/libc base leaks are required only when using addresses from that region. Routes must match pwn_payload_execute launch assumptions. Heap strategies must match the observed libc/glibc allocator version and hardening.
Use observed evidence only. Report blockers instead of inventing facts.
Write payload code only after the exploit route, required bases, offsets, and control/direct-read path are decided.
For exploit success, verify a live command or direct flag output; weak markers are not success.
